82-Pb-208 RPI, LANL EVAL-Aug23 P.J. Brain BNL, NNL DIST-AUG24 REV1-JUL24 20240830 ---- ENDF/B-VIII.1 MATERIAL 8237 REVISION 1 ----- INCIDENT-NEUTRON DATA ------ ENDF-6 ****************************************************************
Resolved Resonance Region Evaluation: 1e-11 to 1.5 MeV
P. Brain*, Y.Danon*, D.Brown", A. Lewis^, and D. Barry^
*Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute Troy, NY 12180, USA brainp@rpi.edu "Brookhaven National Laboratory Upton, NY 11973-5000, USA ^Naval Nuclear Laboratory Schenectady, New York 12301-1072, USA
****************************************************************
The resolved resonance evaluation utilized transmission and capture data sets [ref01-06] in the SAMMY code [ref07].
Base resonance parameters taken from ENDF/B-VIII [ref08]. The effective scattering radius R' was changed to 9.75 fm to get proper potential scattering term [ref09].
Constraining the capture cross section was done with Maxwellian Averaged Cross Sections (MACS) at 30 keV. Work by Beer, Allen [ref10], Weissman [ref11] demonstrated that MACS(30 keV) should be 0.35 mb. Due to the poor capture data on this isotope, many resonance have an average radiation width which was changed to get the above MACS(30 keV). In addition, a direct capture component was added in MF-3. Capture cross section around 10 eV is now 10x greater than ENDF/B-VIII but the average resonance contribution is down by a factor of 2.
The resolved resonance was extended from 1 MeV to 1.5 MeV using Carlton transmission data [ref04] and RPI scattering measurements with nautral lead [ref12]. Due to spin insensitivity of certain transmission energies, a regressive method of spin assignments was developed using SAMMY, NJOY [ref13], and MCNP [ref14]. Cross section integral comparisons were made between R-matrix and pointwise cross sections to ensure no more than 1% in integral cross section was changed as a result of formalism change.
------------------------------------------------------------- Cross Section(2200 m/s) RPI (b) NIST (b) total 11.50 11.34 +/- 0.15 elastic 11.50 11.34 +/- 0.15 capture 0.000235 0.00023 +/- 0.00002 ------------------------------------------------------------- Resonance Integral RPI (b) total 1.39846E+02 elastic 1.39845E+02 capture 7.87194E-04 ------------------------------------------------------------- Scattering Length RPI(fm) NIST (fm) bound coherent 9.55 9.50 +/- 0.06 -------------------------------------------------------------
MF-4 was recalculated from resonance parameters on a high resolution energy grid within the RRR limits using NJOY16[ref13] with Blatt-Biedenharn formalism enabed.
MF-32 was produced with SAMMY.
MF-34 was produced with SAMMY and Python using correlated sampling of MF-32 to create synthetic MF-2 and MF-4.
MF-33 calculated with CoH and KALMAN filter, specifically MT-1,2,4,16,102. ****************************************************************
Fast Region Evaluation: 1.5 to 20 MeV
T.Kawano&, P. Brain*, Y.Danon*, D.Brown", and D. Barry^
*Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute Troy, NY 12180, USA brainp@rpi.edu &Los Alamos National Laboratory Los Alamos,New Mexico 87545, USA "Brookhaven National Laboratory Upton, NY 11973-5000, USA ^Naval Nuclear Laboratory Schenectady, New York 12301-1072, USA
****************************************************************
Full calculation of all reaction channels from threshold to 20 MeV using CoH-3 [ref15] Hauser Feschbach Statistical Code. Kunieda global fit OMP parameters adjusted to fit experimental data [ref03] [ref16]. Coupled channels and DWBA used for inelastic channels with a vibrational deformation model. Resonance structure that could not be resolved but is present in transmission data sets were included to elastic and inelastic partial channels such that the total calculated cross section matches the experimental. Angular distributions for all reactions were calculated from CoH-3.
